props.title: A jazz band for your corporate event, in whatever size you need.
props.lede: Walk into a company event, hear an upright bass and a guitar, and you can tell somebody really thought about this one. That’s what a jazz band does for a corporate event, and it can stay with you from the reception through dinner to the dancing. We can start with a duo and add musicians as the event goes on, playing from the same song list.

headingText.html: You’ll have one contract and a single point of contact for the whole event, and you can learn more about our corporate work, too.

props.title: Jazz for each part of your corporate event.
props.lede: You may want a different amount of music for each part of your event, and none at all during the program.

rows.text: A duo of upright bass and guitar plays jazz standards as your guests arrive. You can tell it’s live from across the venue, and everyone can still talk easily.
A trio adds quiet drums, played with brushes, and it stays soft enough for everyone at the table to talk. Our Changes Jazz Trio is a great choice here if you’d like standards with a more modern edge.
The band plays right up to the moment and then stops before your speaker reaches the microphone. We can also play each winner up to the stage. Check out our run of show planner for more.

When the program ends, the quartet gets people dancing. That’s the trio plus a horn or a singer, playing swing and soul favorites. If your event runs later, a DJ or a covers band can take over for the after-party.

props.title: Corporate events that are a great fit for a jazz band.

rows.text: A duo can play the whole event, and it’s perfect when the conversation is what matters most.
A gala is a great place for a horn, so we often suggest the trio through dinner and the full quartet after the program.
The trio can play drinks and dinner, and then the quartet with a singer or the DJ can get people dancing. In December the Christmas jazz trio plays the season’s songs.
A duo is a lovely choice for a dinner at a mountain lodge.

props.html: Curious about prices? Take a look at what a jazz band costs in Denver. Want something more contemporary than jazz standards? Check out Last Consulate, one musician on upright bass, guitar and electronics playing laid-back instrumental originals.

props.title: What planners ask about corporate jazz bands.

items.q: Which size of jazz band does a corporate event need?
items.a: For a reception or a dinner for up to eighty guests, we’d suggest the duo or the trio. For a ballroom of two hundred, the trio through dinner and the quartet after the program make a great combination, with a horn or a singer out front. Tell us the headcount, the venue and whether the evening has a dance floor, and we'll recommend the size. Signet Artists books jazz bands across Denver and the Colorado mountains.
We can play as softly as you’d like through the reception and dinner. Once the program ends, the quartet can play like a dance band, up to what the venue allows.
Sets can run 45 to 60 minutes, and we can keep music going through the breaks.

items.q: What do you need from us to quote it?
items.a: We just need the date, the venue and a rough idea of the flow of the evening. From there, we’ll recommend a size and send you a price, and we can share the space and power details with your venue.

props.title: Send us the date and we’ll help you find the right size of jazz band for your event.
props.lede: From a solo guitarist to a quartet with a horn, we can put together the jazz band that suits your event, with a sound system sized to your venue.
